//storage: SINGLE OBJECT, NOT AN ARRAY — and the difference is why the emulator would not start.
The ARRAY form is the multi-bucket form: it binds each rules file to a named DEPLOY TARGET,
registered with `firebase target:apply storage <name> <bucket>` and stored in .firebaserc.
No storage target was ever registered — .firebaserc carries two hosting targets and no storage
key at all — so the array had no target to resolve and the emulator refused to start with
The `bucket` key does not satisfy that. It is read on the deploy path, not by the emulator's
rules-config reader, which is why this never surfaced before: `firebase deploy --only storage`
has never successfully run against this project (the previous audit established the Storage
rules have never been deployed, and .firebase/ holds hosting caches only).
The single-object form needs no target: it applies the rules to the project's DEFAULT bucket.
That is the same bucket the array named, which is why this is a fix and not a retarget —
for project `zipper-83816`, and `project_info.storage_bucket` IS the default bucket. The same
name is independently recorded in backend/app/config.py and storage-cors.json.
Nothing about which bucket is governed has changed. The bucket is no longer RESTATED here,
because stating it is what required the target that did not exist.

functions.//: TypeScript is compiled on every deploy. Without this, `firebase deploy --only functions` uploads whatever happens to be in functions/lib and a source change silently does not ship.
functions.//2: The entrance artwork folders are inputs to the one-off upload scripts, not something any function reads at runtime. Without these lines every deploy packed 111 MB of entrance art (102 MB of it image-sequence Lottie JSON) into the function bundle and uploaded it again.
functions.//3: Audit I-9: `.env*` is never part of the uploaded source. The CLI reads functions/.env locally at deploy time and sets the values as environment variables on each function; the file itself has no runtime reader, so excluding it from the archive changes nothing about configuration and stops a key file travelling inside every source bundle. `*.log` covers the firebase-debug logs (kept listed) and anything else a local run leaves behind.

hosting.//: The Android App Links site — the project's DEFAULT hosting site, which is also the Firebase Auth domain (zipper-83816.firebaseapp.com). It serves one file that matters: /.well-known/assetlinks.json.
hosting.//2: It has to be THIS host. Firebase generates the email-binding link on the auth domain, and Android verifies an App Link against assetlinks.json on the host in the link. Until this target existed the host answered 'Site Not Found', so the link opened a browser and the binding never came back to the app.
hosting.//3: IGNORE IS SPELLED OUT, and that is the whole point. Firebase Hosting's DEFAULT ignore list contains '**/.*', which matches every dotted path — including .well-known. Inheriting it would silently drop the one file this target exists to publish, deploy successfully, and leave a 404 with nothing in the log to explain it.

headers.//: Android will not accept the file without this content type. Firebase infers it from the extension here, but the file has no extension in the URL path people test with, so it is stated rather than assumed.

Audit C-7 / I-13: security headers on every response of the CRM site. `frame-ancestors 'none'` (and X-Frame-Options for older browsers) stops the CRM being framed; nosniff, Referrer-Policy and HSTS are the usual hardening. The CSP is CONSERVATIVE and every origin in it is derived from the code — see the //csp-origins note below. The /api/** rewrite is same-origin, so 'self' covers the Cloud Run API.
//csp-origins: 'self' — the static export, the /api/** Cloud Run rewrite (same origin), and locally-bundled Firebase SDK.
script-src 'unsafe-inline' — Next.js static export inlines its hydration/RSC payload scripts; a static host cannot mint nonces. 'wasm-unsafe-eval' — Agora RTC SDK processing modules on /live.

https://apis.google.com, https://www.gstatic.com, https://www.google.com — Firebase Auth Google sign-in (signInWithPopup loads gapi) and invisible reCAPTCHA for phone linking (components/ContactVerificationPanel.tsx).
https://download.agora.io — the Agora RTC SDK script for the moderation live player (components/LiveWatch.tsx AGORA_SDK_URL).
https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com — lottie-web (bodymovin) for gift/entrance previews (components/LottieThumb.tsx, AnimationThumb.tsx, public/lottie-test.html).
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net, https://unpkg.com — svgaplayerkit for SVGA previews (components/AnimationThumb.tsx, with unpkg as the fallback).

connect-src https://*.googleapis.com — Firebase Auth (identitytoolkit, securetoken), Firestore (firestore.googleapis.com), Storage (firebasestorage.googleapis.com), signed Storage URLs (storage.googleapis.com) and the Google people API behind Google sign-in.
connect-src https://*.firebaseio.com / wss://*.firebaseio.com — Firebase SDK realtime channel (kept for the SDK's own fallbacks; nothing in the CRM reads RTDB directly).

connect-src https://*.cloudfunctions.net — httpsCallable(getFunctions(app, 'asia-south1')) for generateAgoraToken and the email-code callables (components/LiveWatch.tsx, ContactVerificationPanel.tsx).

connect-src/frame-src https://zipper-83816.firebaseapp.com — the Firebase Auth domain (NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN): the sign-in popup handler and its hidden iframe. If the auth domain is ever changed, change it here too.
connect-src https://open.er-api.com — exchange rates for the local-prices preview (components/LocalPricesModal.tsx).
connect-src https://*.agora.io, wss://*.agora.io, https://*.sd-rtn.com, wss://*.sd-rtn.com — Agora RTC signalling and gateway for the live player.
connect-src https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net, https://unpkg.com — the same CDNs, for source maps and fetch()-based loaders in the players.

img-src/media-src https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com, https://storage.googleapis.com — uploaded documents, proofs, gift artwork and entrance videos; img-src https://*.googleusercontent.com — Google account photos on profiles.
frame-src https://www.google.com, https://recaptcha.google.com, https://accounts.google.com — reCAPTCHA and Google sign-in frames.
NOT allowed on purpose: any other third-party origin, inline event handlers beyond what Next emits, eval. A new external origin must be added here with the file that needs it.

headers.//: Hashed Next.js assets are immutable; HTML is not (it names the hashes).

rewrites.//: Python API on Cloud Run, served from the same origin so there is no CORS.
rewrites.//2: Must come first — anything under /api/ goes to the backend, not the SPA.

rewrites./: next.config.js sets trailingSlash: true, so the real path is /agencies/<id>/salary/ — a pattern ending at 'salary' never matched and fell through to /agencies/**, serving the agency detail page under the salary URL.
